transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-18 | Start: 16:00 UTC | Duration: 52m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Eli Vargas (Redwood SE), Anika Patel (Head of Platform, CedarBridge), Gareth O'Neil (CCO, CedarBridge), Luis Romero (Infra), Priya Nair (Legal - partial)

Summary:
CedarBridge is evaluating Redwood for customer-facing Q&A and accounting reconciliation assistants. Primary concerns: strict data residency in EU and UK, long-term archival / records retention for financial audits (~7 years), log retention and sanitization (no raw PII leaves region), KMS key residency/escrow, and proof of SOC2/ISO controls. Customer leaning toward Dedicated or Private deployment but wants to understand tradeoffs and what can remain hosted with controls.

Topics covered:
- Residency options (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)
- Audit log retention and redaction strategies
- KMS and key residency / HSM options
- Network controls: VPC peering, private link, and egress restrictions
- Compliance artifacts and evidence (SOC2, ISO, penetration test summaries)
- Benchmarks and performance expectations for privacy-preserving configurations

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros — I'm Maya, AE, and Eli's our solutions engineer.
[00:12] Anika (CedarBridge): Hi, Anika here — platform. We have Gareth, Luis, and Priya who will pop in for legal bits.
[00:17] Gareth (CedarBridge CCO): Hey all. We're mainly focused on residency and retention — lots of regulators asking for explicit retention windows and auditable chains.
[00:25] Eli (Redwood SE): Great, we'll walk through how Redwood surfaces residency and retention controls across hosted, dedicated, and private. Note, I might refer to our Dedicated offering as "Redwood Dedication" sometimes — sorry, habit.
[00:38] Luis: Quick thing — our architecture currently lives in eu-west-1 and eu-west-2, all customer data must stay in EU or UK zones. We can't have logs or backups leaving region unless anonymized.
[00:48] Maya: Understood. High level: Hosted can be region-locked for EU-only, but metadata leakage and some support workflows may still require controlled access by Redwood staff. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools in region + stronger isolation. Private (VPC or on-prem) gives you full control — control plane in your environment, customer-managed networking and keys.
[01:05] Gareth: On control plane — for Private, is the control plane fully customer-managed or do you run any components?
[01:09] Eli: For our Private package the control plane can be customer-managed, yes. We ship an on-prem operator that runs in your cluster, or for VPC it's a private control plane that we can host inside your cloud account. Nothing leaves the region unless you opt in for diagnostic uploads.
[01:24] Priya (Legal, off-mic): Sorry running a quick conflict, I'm on.
[01:27] Maya: No problem. Luis, you mentioned logs — can you describe what you consider "logs" for regs? Is it application-level traces, raw request/response, or aggregated telemetry?
[01:36] Luis: Regs want message-level provenance for audits — not necessarily full PII but an auditable sequence. They also want ability to produce redacted transcripts on demand.
[01:44] Eli: We have a few patterns: 1) Keep full logs in customer-managed storage (S3) in the region and push only aggregated metrics to Redwood; 2) Token-level or request-level logs can be routed to a customer-owned logging endpoint; 3) For Hosted where that's not possible, we support pseudonymization and field-level redaction before logs leave region.
[02:02] Anika: Is there a way to let Redwood's console/observability access things without copying raw logs out of our account? We still want token-level cost breakdowns per route.
[02:12] Maya: Yes — for Dedicated/Private we can stream traces and metrics to your telemetry (Datadog/in-house) and only surface aggregated breakdowns in the Redwood Console via API proxies. The console can be configured to query metrics via a read-only endpoint in your VPC.
[02:28] Gareth: What about key management — keys must be retained in our HSM in EU, no key material leaving the region. Can Redwood integrate with our KMS/HSM?
[02:36] Eli: Absolutely. We support customer-managed keys via KMS (bring-your-own-KMS) and can integrate with cloud KMS offerings and external HSMs. For Private deployments the encryption keys never leave your environment. For Dedicated we can support BYOK where the keys are in your cloud KMS and Redwood instances use them via IAM roles and limited ephemeral access.
[02:56] Luis: Does that cover model weights or just data at rest? We have vendors who insist that model telemetry or weights are sometimes pulled for patches.
[03:04] Eli: Model weights are part of the runtime image. For Private/on-prem we ship images that you host; for Dedicated we can pin model versions to ensure no external fetches. For Hosted, models are in Redwood's catalog — we can provide attestations of versioning.
[03:20] Anika: Our compliance team is nervous about logs containing raw PII — typical user utterances can include name, account numbers. We need a way to redact automatically and still be able to produce an auditor-facing record.
[03:31] Maya: Two options: inline redaction — we run a pre-processor that strips or masks PII before hitting the runtime; or store full transcripts encrypted in your in-region storage and provide an auditor-only decryption workflow with strict access controls. Which would you prefer?
[03:45] Gareth: Auditor-only decryption is appealing because we can show provenance. But we also need an immutable audit trail for regulatory purposes — WORM-like retention.
[03:53] Eli: We support WORM retention policies on customer-managed storage and can integrate with object-lock in S3 to enforce immutability for configured windows (e.g., 7 years).
[04:02] Luis: About access controls — we need RBAC integration with our SSO (SAML/Okta). Can Redwood map roles to console actions and to the API?
[04:10] Maya: Yes — we support SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, and RBAC that's configurable per-route and per-model. For Private we can integrate with your internal identity provider and honor group-based permissions.
[04:21] Priya: Legal question — what about subpoenas? If logs are hosted by Redwood, what's your policy on turning data over?
[04:28] Eli: We only respond per our MSA and applicable jurisdictional requirements. With Private/on-prem the customer retains the logs. With Dedicated we'll follow the data access policies in the contract; hosted is the riskiest in this respect because Redwood may be subject to foreign legal process. We'll flag that in the RACI.
[04:45] Anika: Performance note — we expect sub-300ms latency for small prompts. Does residency / encryption affect that?
[04:52] Eli: Encryption at rest doesn't; network path and routing will. Private in-region deployments will meet your latency SLOs. Batching and KV cache usage can improve throughput but must be tuned to keep latency tight. There is a trade-off: synchronous high QPS with small tokens favors Dedicated/Private.
[05:10] Maya: Do you anticipate needing full model finetuning or are you using out-of-the-box open models?
[05:14] Anika: Likely out-of-the-box with light instruction tuning; we want to avoid persisting customer corpus unless required for retraining.
[05:20] Eli: Good — that reduces persistence exposure. If you do want to persist training data, we can store it in your controlled store and never export.
[05:28] Luis: A tricky ask — we must prove to auditors that no raw payment card data was stored. Do you offer PCI-DSS focused redaction or guards?
[05:36] Maya: We don't claim PCI compliance as a product (we do have SOC 2 and ISO artifacts). For PCI you would typically want Private or Dedicated with strict redaction preprocessors and controls to avoid card storage; we can work with your PCI assessor.
[05:50] Gareth: On logging retention durations — regulators here ask for seven years of certain records. Does Redwood support granular retention per-data-class?
[05:58] Eli: Yes — retention policies can be per-bucket/per-data-class. You can set different WORM windows and tie retention to labels on requests. We can also auto-redact sensitive fields after a window.
[06:12] Anika: Can you show the console's audit trail? Our auditors want to see who accessed what and when.
[06:18] Maya: Console audit logs are exportable to your SIEM and we can keep access logs in-region for the retention window you specify.
[06:26] Luis: About telemetry — we don't want full transcripts in logs but want request IDs to trace back when needed. Is there a way to link a request ID to an auditor-only store?
[06:36] Eli: Yes — we recommend storing a GUID request ID in visibility layers. The auditor-only store keeps the mapping and you control decryption keys.
[06:45] Anika: Any red flags around backups? Some vendors replicate backups cross-region by default. We must keep backups in-region.
[06:53] Eli: For Dedicated/Private we can enforce in-region backups. For Hosted we can configure region-scoped backups but need contract language to prevent cross-region replication.
[07:03] Gareth: About evidence — we need to see pen-test outputs and change control evidence.
[07:09] Maya: We'll share redwood-security-pack.pdf which contains SOC2 Type II results, a pen-test summary (redacted), patching cadence, and our change control policy.
[07:20] Priya: On legal, can you provide sample MSA language around log retention, data ownership, and key escrow?
[07:27] Maya: Yes, we'll provide sample clauses and a proposed MSA addendum for log residency and key management.
[07:33] Luis: Technical deep-dive — when you say "KV cache" how is that persisted? Does the KV cache ever touch disk?
[07:40] Eli: Our KV cache is memory-first, but under memory pressure we may spill to local disk. For Private deployments that disk is in your environment and can be encrypted and bound to the host. We can also configure cache eviction to avoid persistent disk spill if that's unacceptable.
[07:58] Anika: Could you run a redaction demo or sample pipeline? Seeing it flow would help.
[08:03] Eli: Sure, we can do a 30m demo. We'll set up a pipeline that runs PII detection using regex + NER and shows redacted vs raw storage options.
[08:12] Maya: We'll also include a sample benchmark spreadsheet with latency numbers for EU region under a redaction pipeline.
[08:18] Gareth: One more thing — incident response. If there's a breach, what's the notification SLA and who has to be notified?
[08:25] Eli: Our SR includes incident notification timelines; for Dedicated/Private we can agree to stricter SLAs in the contract. We'll provide our incident playbook and expected timelines.
[08:36] Luis: About metrics — we want per-route token cost visibility but must avoid storing raw tokens. Do you support tokenized billing without content?
[08:45] Maya: Yes — cost/invoice can be driven by token counts and request metadata without persisting content. Billing records can omit content payloads and be available in-region.
[08:54] Anika: If we choose Dedicated with BYOK, do you manage the infra or do we? We need clarity for operations.
[08:59] Eli: Dedicated is typically co-managed — Redwood operates the runtime but the infrastructure (VPC, subnet, KMS) is your responsibility. We offer optional managed services where we take on more ops responsibility under an SLA.
[09:12] Maya: Let's surface decisions: sounds like CID wants Private or Dedicated due to residency and retention. Is that right?
[09:18] Gareth: Yes leaning Private, but we need to validate costs and support model. Also legal wants MSA redlines before committing.
[09:25] Maya: Next steps recap: I'll share SOC2 + ISO artifacts and security pack. Eli will share architecture diagram and schedule a redaction demo + benchmark. Legal will get sample MSA clauses. Luis will share log samples.
[09:36] Priya: We'll set up a follow-up with our procurement and legal in two weeks.
[09:40] Maya: Great — any final quick questions?
[09:43] Anika: One misc: are snapshots encrypted with customer keys?
[09:46] Eli: Yes — snapshots and backups can be encrypted with your KMS keys.
[09:50] Gareth: That covers most. Thanks all.
[09:53] Maya: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with artifacts by Friday.

(End of meeting)
